about_description: AWS Gateway brings selected Amazon S3 and Amazon EC2 functionality together and provides an overview of resource usage, costs and activity.
about_storage_contents: Stored here: the database, saved AWS profiles, the activity log and application settings.
about_storage_not_saved: Not stored: the secret key, or temporary credentials obtained through role login (AssumeRole) - these are entered, or fetched, on every login and are never written to disk.
about_license_aws_sdk: AWS SDK for .NET (Apache 2.0) - Communication with AWS services within the gateway.
about_license_dapper: Dapper (Apache 2.0) - Mapping SQL queries and results from the local database.
about_license_sqlite: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite (MIT) - Local SQLite database for profiles, settings and activity logs.
about_license_itext: iText (AGPL or commercial license) - Generating PDF reports.
help_ch_getting_started_body:
1. Local account: on your first login, enter a username and password - the account is created automatically. The password needs at least 6 characters and at least one digit.

2. AWS keys: enter your AWS user's Access Key and Secret Key, or use role login (see below).

3. Profile: turn on "Save settings as profile" so next time you don't have to re-enter the region, keys and other details - the secret key itself is never saved.

4. Role login and MFA: turn on "Use IAM role (AssumeRole)" and enter the role ARN. If the role requires MFA, also enter the MFA device's serial number and the current MFA code. A session logged in via a role has a limited duration, and you'll need to log in again once it expires.
help_ch_home_body:
Home gives a quick overview of the current state, drawn only from data already available on this computer (no new AWS calls):

• Session - login mode, remaining time (for role login) and region.
• AWS account - account number and identity, with a copy button.
• Local service - status of the TCP server used for team activity.
• Recent transfers - the last 5 transfers, with a link to the full history in Reports.
• This month's cost - from the cache, with a comparison to last month if available.
• Recent activity - the last 5 entries from your own activity log.
help_ch_s3_body:
1. Pick a bucket from the list, or type a name and click Refresh to load it.

2. Objects in the bucket appear in the table - filter them by name using the search field.

3. Select one or more objects and click Download to save them to your computer.

4. For a temporary sharing link: pick a duration and click Generate link - the link is copied to clipboard automatically, and the Copy button below lets you copy it again.

5. Delete permanently removes the selected objects - confirm the action in the dialog that opens.

6. Uploading files: click Upload and pick files. Advanced settings (part size, concurrent transfers) available via arrow next to Upload.
help_ch_ec2_body:
1. The instance list loads automatically - select an instance to Start, Stop or Reboot it.

2. For a usage assessment: pick a period and click Analyze. The application fetches CloudWatch metrics (CPU, network) and gives a recommendation - whether the instance is idle, moderately used, or overloaded.

3. The raw measurement points are shown in the table below as supporting evidence for the assessment.
help_ch_costs_body:
1. Pick a period (this month, last month, last 30 days) and click Load.

2. Data is looked up in the cache first, since calling AWS Cost Explorer isn't free - Force refresh bypasses the cache and fetches the latest data.

3. The chart shows daily cost, and the tables show a breakdown by service and region - selecting a service in the table fills in the regional breakdown for that service.

4. If Cost Explorer isn't available due to missing permissions, you'll see a corresponding message - see the "Common problems" chapter.
help_ch_reports_body:
1. Filter the transfer list by direction, status, bucket, period or search text.

2. The summary cards show total count, success rate, total data transferred and average speed.

3. Open folder opens the local folder for the file from selected transfer.

4. Delete from history permanently removes selected records from database (doesn't affect files).

5. Export CSV and Export PDF export the currently filtered transfer list.
help_ch_profiles_body:
1. The table shows your saved profiles and older profiles with no owner.

2. New profile: click New, fill in the details and Save. The secret key isn't entered here - you enter it on every login.

3. Select an existing profile to edit it, or Delete to remove it permanently.
help_ch_team_body:
1. Check server checks whether the local TCP server is reachable.

2. The table shows the activity of every team member sharing the same server, along with a per-session log.

3. This feature requires the TCP server to be running - if it isn't available, see the Common problems chapter.
help_ch_settings_body:
1. Language and theme take effect immediately once saved and apply to the whole application.

2. The cost cache TTL sets how long Cost Explorer data is considered fresh before it's fetched again.

3. Delete account permanently deletes your local account and all your saved profiles - this action can't be undone.
help_ch_problems_body:
"Wrong password" - check upper/lower case; the password needs at least 6 characters and at least one digit.

"Wrong AWS data" - check the Access Key and Secret Key, and whether they match the role or user you're using.

"Session expired" - role login (AssumeRole) has a limited duration. Log in again.

"Bucket list unavailable" - the role or user in use doesn't have the s3:ListAllMyBuckets permission. Type the bucket name manually.

"Cost Explorer unavailable" - the ce:GetCostAndUsage permission is required. Contact your AWS account administrator.

"Server unavailable" - the local TCP server (Team status) isn't running, or is blocked by a firewall.
help_ch_security_body:
Stored: username, saved AWS profiles (name, region, Access Key, role ARN), the activity log and application settings.

Not stored: the secret key, or temporary credentials obtained through role login (AssumeRole) - these are entered, or fetched, on every login and are never written to disk.

Session expiry: role login has a limited duration set by the AWS role. When it expires, the application automatically returns you to the login screen without losing your saved profiles. Access-key login has no session expiry within the application.
